summary: Over the next 12 months, AI is shifting from raw model scale toward intelligence quality: reasoning models that trade speed for accuracy, agentic systems that execute long-running workflows, and multimodal understanding becoming table stakes. Simultaneously, inference costs are falling roughly 10x per year, open-weight models (led by Chinese labs like Alibaba's Qwen and Moonshot's Kimi) are closing the gap with proprietary systems, and distributed AI 'superfactories' plus physical/robotics AI are emerging as the next frontiers.

trends.name: Reasoning Models (Inference-Time Compute Scaling)
trends.description: Models that spend more compute at test time to 'think' before answering via chain-of-thought and reinforcement learning, trading latency for substantially higher accuracy on hard tasks. Reinforcement learning is increasingly used to make models reason and use tools strategically.
trends.why_it_matters: It dramatically improves reliability on complex math, coding, and scientific tasks, making AI usable for high-stakes reasoning work.

trends.name: Agentic & Multi-Agent Systems
trends.description: AI architectures where autonomous agents plan, use tools, and coordinate across multiple specialized agents to complete multi-step workflows. These systems now feature memory, self-critique, and dynamic agent assignment within orchestrated workflows.
trends.why_it_matters: Agents move AI from single-turn chat to executing real business processes end-to-end with minimal human intervention.

trends.name: Persistent / Long-Running Agents
trends.description: Agents that handle longer workflows over extended periods, maintain long-term memory, and increasingly run locally on-device. They leverage context engineering and vector-database memory retrieval to sustain state across sessions.
trends.why_it_matters: Persistent agents enable AI to own long-horizon projects rather than one-off tasks, unlocking true workflow automation.

trends.name: Multimodal Models (Vision-Language-Audio Fusion)
trends.description: Models that integrate text, vision, audio, and video into a joint latent representation, making multimodal understanding standard at the frontier. Seamless fusion of different media is now a defining capability of leading models.
trends.why_it_matters: Multimodality lets AI perceive and act on the real world across documents, images, screens, and speech in one system.

trends.name: AI Coding Agents
trends.description: Agentic tools that read, write, test, and refactor code across entire repositories rather than autocompleting single lines. They combine reasoning models with tool use and long context to deliver production software changes.
trends.why_it_matters: Coding agents are the fastest-monetizing AI application, measurably accelerating software development across the industry.

trends.name: Open-Weight Model Parity
trends.description: Open-weight models are rapidly closing the gap with proprietary systems, driven by global model diversification and Chinese multilingual, reasoning-tuned releases. Full weights and training details are increasingly published, strengthening the open ecosystem.
trends.why_it_matters: Open parity drives down costs, boosts customization, and shifts competitive dynamics across the US and Chinese AI labs.

trends.name: Inference Cost Collapse
trends.description: The cost of a given capability is falling roughly 10x per year through better hardware, distillation, and architectural efficiency. This makes frontier-level intelligence economically viable at massive scale.
trends.why_it_matters: Plummeting inference cost turns experimental AI features into always-on, mass-deployed products.

trends.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP) & Standard Agent Toolkits
trends.description: Standardized protocols and SDKs that let agents connect to tools, data sources, and runtimes through shared interfaces. Interoperability is becoming a competitive axis as frameworks align around common standards.
trends.why_it_matters: Shared standards make agents composable and portable, accelerating a plug-and-play agent ecosystem.

trends.name: Computer Use / UI Agents
trends.description: Agents that operate graphical user interfaces by viewing screens and controlling mouse and keyboard to complete tasks in arbitrary software. They combine multimodal perception with agentic planning to automate human-facing applications.
trends.why_it_matters: UI agents unlock automation of any software without APIs, dramatically widening the scope of what AI can do.

trends.name: Physical AI & Robotics
trends.description: A shift in research priorities toward embodied, 'palpable' AI as robotics and physical AI pick up momentum. Foundation models are increasingly applied to perception, control, and manipulation in the physical world.
trends.why_it_matters: Physical AI extends LLM-driven intelligence from screens into factories, warehouses, and homes.

trends.name: Small Language Models (SLMs) & Edge AI
trends.description: Compact, distilled models optimized to run locally on phones, laptops, and edge devices while retaining strong reasoning for targeted tasks. They enable private, low-latency inference without cloud dependence.
trends.why_it_matters: SLMs bring capable AI to offline, private, and cost-sensitive deployments at the edge.

trends.name: Distributed AI Superfactories
trends.description: A new generation of linked AI data centers that pack computing power densely across distributed networks to drive down costs and improve efficiency. Infrastructure is being reorganized into flexible, global AI systems.
trends.why_it_matters: It reshapes AI economics by making training and serving globally scalable and more efficient.
